title: Kayaking the Mangroves at Balandra
coverImageAlt: Placeholder — real mangrove kayaking photo to come
excerpt: The channel narrows enough in places that you can touch both banks of mangrove without really trying.
subtitle: Playa Balandra closes to boats some afternoons. The mangroves just inland don't care either way.
author: Flavia Ibarra
body:
Balandra is one of the more protected coves we anchor near, which means restrictions on where boats can go that don't apply to a kayak. We'll paddle in through the mangrove channels on the days conditions allow it.

It's a different kind of quiet than open water. The mangroves cut the wind almost completely, and the channel narrows enough in places that you're paddling through a tunnel of roots rather than across open water.

> You go from open bay to something that feels almost like a jungle river in about two hundred meters.

![Placeholder — real photo of the mangrove channel at low tide to come](/assets/photos/source/whale-shark.jpg "Paddling the mangrove channel at low tide, when the roots show most.")

Low tide is the better time to go, when more of the root system is exposed and the small fish that shelter there are easier to see from the kayak.

It's a short trip, usually under an hour, but it's the part of the day people ask the most questions about afterward.
